notes.decision: = ⲙⲛⲧϣⲙⲏⲛ 'eight' (cardinal-abstract). Lyc. ⲝ for ⲧϣ regular dialectal sandhi. Chapter heading: 'the Eight Great Thrones of all the Fathers.'
= ⲥⲟⲟⲩ 'six' (Lyc. ϯⲥ regular). Six of the eight thrones are set in the outer aeons; by implication two remain in the inner Greatness — the first being the Father's throne (line 29ff).

Translated tentatively 'the Half (Region).' ⲡⲁⲥⲉ may be Lyc. ⲡⲁϣ 'half, division' or a specific cosmological region. The phrase 'in all the worlds of ⲡⲁⲥⲉ' designates the cosmological domain in which the six outer thrones reside. Confidence low; flag for parallels.

'In his own essence, by himself.' ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ = οὐσία (per terminology guide: 'substance/essence'). Here in apophatic context of the Father's throne: he sits alone in his own substance, by himself, upon himself — the absolute self-grounding of the divine throne.
ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ from ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ 'pass over, surpass, transcend' (cf. ⲟⲩⲱⲑ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in glossary). The first throne is 'the one which surpasses all (other) thrones' — hierarchic supremacy of the Father's throne.

Reading as ⲡⲉⲧⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ split across line break (line 3 ends ⲡⲉ ⲡⲉ-, line 4 begins -ⲧⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ): 'the Established One of the Father.' This is a substantival qualitative epithet for the First Man, parallel to ⲡⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ ('the standing-fast') as a stable foundational figure. Translating as 'Established One' (capitalized title) preserves both the verbal-foundational sense and the appositional structure.

Verb ⲫⲃ̄ⲟ unattested in accumulated vocabulary. Most likely Lyc. reflex of ϥⲃⲟ 'lessen, weaken, abolish' (Crum 619a) or ⲫⲱⲃ 'destroy.' Context: First Man encountering 'the foremost of all Enmity' in the worlds of Darkness — the primordial Manichaean cosmic combat. 'Subdued' chosen as preserving both the martial and weakening senses. Alternative 'vanquished' or 'extinguished' also possible.

ⲙⲁⲙⲟⲩⲣ analyzed as compound ⲙⲁ- ('place of') + ⲙⲟⲩⲣ ('binding') = 'place of binding.' Paired here with Greek loanword σφυλακή/φυλακή ('prison-house, guardpost') in hendiadys describing the Great Builder's cosmic prison for the Enemy and his powers. The doublet renders both the architectural-binding and the custodial functions of the cosmic structure.

ϩⲱⲣⲃ̄ likely Lyc. variant cognate with ϩⲃⲟⲣⲃⲣ̄/ϩⲃⲱⲣⲃ̄ 'cast down, throw down' (cf. accumulated ⲑⲃⲓⲟ 'humble' and the parallel ⲍⲃⲱⲣⲃ̄). Context fits Manichaean cosmogony: the Living Spirit cast down the dark archons and used their bodies to construct the cosmos ('established the worlds'). 'Cast down' preserves the martial-cosmogonic sense.

ⲙⲣ̄ⲡⲉ read as variant of ⲙⲣ̄ⲣⲉ 'bond, fettering' (Crum 181a). The structure ⲕⲁⲑⲁⲣⲓⲥⲙⲟⲥ ⲙⲉⲛ ... ⲙⲣ̄ⲡⲉ ⲁⲉ provides the Manichaean cosmogonic dyad: the cosmos is BOTH a purification of Light AND a fettering of dark powers. 'Fettering' chosen over 'bond' to preserve the active-restraining sense.

ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ here = ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'king' (cf. accumulated ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ 'be king/reign'); ⲧϩⲱⲛⲏ = the Zone (= Greek ζώνη), the zodiacal-cosmic girdle. The Third Ambassador is technically titled 'King of the Zone' in Manichaean cosmology — he rules the zodiacal sphere from the sun-ship. Departing from accumulated 'prison/fastness' for ⲧϩⲱⲛⲏ here because the Zone-as-zodiac reading is overwhelming in this throne-enumeration context (cf. ⲧⲍⲱⲛⲏ in vocabulary).

ⲕⲱⲗ + directional ⲁⲣⲁϩ ('to him') — verb ⲕⲱⲗ likely 'roll up, gather, wrap' (Crum 100a). The image is of the Life of the saved being rolled/gathered up to the Great Mind as the cosmic gatherer. Translating 'is gathered up to him' preserves both the unitive and directional motion characteristic of Manichaean ascent vocabulary.

Literal: 'that of the Great One of the Spirit.' In the day-ship enumeration this is the second throne, between the Third Ambassador (1st) and the Living Spirit (3rd). 'Great One of the Spirit' is unusual as a separate title — it likely designates an emanation or aspect distinct from the Living Spirit proper. Possibly the Mother of the Living, or a peri­phrastic designation for the Spirit-Mind. Translating literally to preserve the ambiguity rather than identify with another known figure.

Translated as 'throne' = Greek θρόνος. Confirmed by line 12 spelling ⲫⲣⲟⲛⲟⲥ which preserves the rho. The sequence describes the cosmic thrones of the great divine beings: Great King of Honor in the 7th firmament, Judge of Truth in the air, Apostle in the holy Church — all standard Manichaean cosmological figures who occupy specific cosmic seats.

Translated 'the sixth' (= ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲟⲟⲩ). The sequence demands an ordinal: line 1 X-th throne in the 2nd Ship, line 2 7th throne in 7th firmament, line 4 8th throne in air, line 8 9th throne in church. Line 12 confirms 'these are the [nine] great thrones.' ⲧⲧⲓⲥⲁⲩ thus = 'the sixth,' a non-standard Lyc form perhaps with article ⲧ- + ⲧⲓⲥⲁⲩ (= ⲡⲥⲟⲟⲩ '6').

'The Great King of Honor' — standard Manichaean cosmological figure who occupies the seventh (highest) firmament. ⲡⲛⲁⲃ = ⲛⲟϭ 'great' (in glossary as 'great' / ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲃ 'lordship'); ⲛ̄ⲣⲡⲟ = 'of king(s)' (cf. ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ 'reign'); ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲟ = 'honor.'

'The Judge of Truth' (κριτὴς τῆς ἀληθείας) — standard Manichaean cosmological figure stationed in the air, who judges human souls after death and divides them into three paths (death, life, agreement) as line 7 specifies.

Translated 'to the agreement' / 'to joining.' ⲡⲧⲱⲧ from ⲧⲱⲧ 'be joined' — already in glossary as 'the agreement / accord.' In the standard Manichaean post-mortem schema: souls go either to Light (ⲡⲱⲛⲍ 'life'), to Hell (ⲡⲙⲟⲩ 'death'), or to a third middle state — for catechumens, often described as 'reconciliation' or 'mixing.' 'Agreement' preserves the verbal-joining root.
'The ninth.' Final element ϯⲥ = ⲯⲓⲥ '9.' Confirmed by line 12 [ⲡϯⲥ] 'the nine.'

'The apostle who has come to our feet at this time' — i.e. Mani himself, the present apostolic incarnation. ⲍⲓⲣⲉⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ uses the idiom ⲍⲓⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'unto the feet of' (in glossary) with -ⲧⲏⲛⲉ 'us' (Lyc 1pl). The 9th throne is thus the present Manichaean Church itself, with Mani as its enthroned Judge of Righteousness.
